versions.short: The bill would convey roughly 1,270 acres of federal land and about half an acre of federal land to Carson City, Nevada, at no cost to the city, with the city paying the associated costs and the land reverting to the United States if it stops being used for public purposes. It would also require the federal government to sell about 356 acres of federal land to qualified bidders, and would transfer roughly 21 and 24 acres from the city to the federal government, with the city keeping certain utility and access rights. Proceeds from these land sales would go into a special account used to repay costs of preparing the sales and to buy environmentally sensitive land in the city. Finally, the bill would amend the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 to adjust how certain city lands are managed and allow the city to enter agreements with third parties for recreational operations.
